name: Person Dignity Theory
summary: Person Dignity Theory (Nhân vị) is the Vietnamese form of Emmanuel Mounier's communitarian personalism, developed by Ngô Đình Nhu in the 1950s as the official doctrine of the Cần Lao Party and Ngô Đình Diệm's South Vietnam. It claims a middle path between capitalism, which it says treats people as consumers, and communism, which treats them as production tools, and it puts the person, with material and spiritual dimensions, at the centre. In practice it was joined to Confucian and Catholic ethics, nationalism, anti-communism and a dominant-party, vanguard-style state.
scope: The doctrine as promoted in the Republic of Vietnam, 1954-1963, by Nhu, Diệm and the Cần Lao Party, drawing on Mounier's personalism, missionary and Catholic-labour thought and Confucian ideas. It excludes French and other personalisms as such, except where they shaped Nhu's version. The doctrine's own writings are thinly available, so many answers are inferred from its principles and from the regime's documented practice, and are marked low.

keyFigures.name: Ngô Đình Nhu
keyFigures.role: Developed the doctrine in the 1950s and founded the Cần Lao Party.

keyFigures.name: Ngô Đình Diệm
keyFigures.role: President of South Vietnam who adopted it as the national ideology.

keyFigures.name: Emmanuel Mounier
keyFigures.role: French philosopher whose personalism was the main Western influence.

sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Mounier's personalism: state for persons, relational person, opposition to individualism, collectivism and Marxism, intrinsic dignity.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Inferred from the personalist concern with the material as well as spiritual needs of the person; none of the sources discuss health care.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from Nhu's complaint that workers under liberalism are left isolated and at the mercy of the rich; wage floors are my extrapolation.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Nhu faulted liberalism for setting no limits on the economic conditions of freedom, so a doctrine of unregulated market allocation is not his.

public-ownership.rationale: Its economic program favoured cooperatives and co-management of industry rather than state ownership, so nationalising utilities is inferred to be unwelcome.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from the critique that the rich dominate isolated workers; no tax program is documented in the sources.

unions-good.rationale: The Cần Lao allied with a trade unionist and its journal endorsed unionization rights and worker cooperatives.

property-fundamental.rationale: Personalism criticises capitalist property in favour of a 'human' property (Mounier's 1936 title listed in the article), so near-absolute property rights are inferred to be rejected.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred from Nhu's view that liberal freedom lacks limits on economic power; specific regulation is not documented.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from personalism's concern for persons in material want and its rejection of unconstrained individualism.

worker-ownership.rationale: Workers' and farmers' cooperatives were endorsed, but the sources describe co-management with capitalists as the program, so collective ownership is only partly supported.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The party built secret networks and a special security force against communist subversion, which implies acceptance of surveillance; the doctrine itself is silent.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's emphasis on moderation and spiritual discipline.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's moral-order emphasis; the sources do not discuss hate speech.

strong-leader.rationale: The regime paired a dominant party with a strong presidency and called its principle 'centralized democracy'.

state-harmful.rationale: Personalism holds that the state exists to serve persons, which presupposes a state; the regime itself was an intensive state-building project.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from order-minded, anti-individualist outlook; no source discusses firearms.

empower-police-military.rationale: The party placed its members in army and security posts and set up a special force against communist infiltration.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from Catholic-Confucian moral conservatism in the doctrine's make-up.

decide-locally.rationale: The regime's 'centralized democracy' and party cell structure favoured national direction over local autonomy.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the inviolable dignity of every person, which personalists hold even for offenders.

traditional-family.rationale: The family is the first community in the person-community dimension and ancestor veneration was fused into the doctrine.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic and Confucian family ethic underlying the doctrine; not addressed directly.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic personalist premise of inviolable personal dignity; not discussed in the sources.

more-religion-public.rationale: The doctrine's supernatural dimension aims to strengthen belief, and Nhu viewed it as originally Catholic though universal.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; its anti-colonial concern is balanced by no documented position on racial remediation.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's natural-order, family-centred anthropology.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Vietnamization of personalism and stress on national spirit and bloodline consciousness made cultural continuity central.

gradual-change.rationale: Nhu and the party described their program as a 'personalist revolution', not gradual institutional continuity.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from the stress on national survival and lineage; immigration was not a live question.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred from nationalist emphasis, though it built transnational anti-communist fraternities.

free-trade.rationale: Inferred from its critique of liberal economics; trade policy is not discussed.

nation-first.rationale: Inferred from the weight on national spirit and survival.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Personalists stress human dignity but the sources give no view on armed intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred from the national-survival and bloodline emphasis.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred from Mounier-style criticism of 'having' over 'being', though no environmental position is documented.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; the Three Humanities include harmony with nature but no policy position is recorded.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Personalism holds that material progress alone leaves people in need of spiritual fulfilment.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed and nothing in the principles points either way.

revolution-justified.rationale: Nhu and the Cần Lao openly promoted a 'personalist revolution' to be carried out by workers.

experts-over-public.rationale: The party was run by an intellectual cadre that trained officials in doctrine; inferred preference for guided rule.

central-planning.rationale: Nhu condemned communism for repressing everyone under a collective economy.

socialized-markets.rationale: Cooperatives and co-management fit the idea, though the doctrine never endorsed public ownership of markets.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not discussed; nothing in the principles favours or opposes it.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from its concern over domination by the rich.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred from the stress on work and responsibility; not discussed.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred from the nation-building aim of the Economy pillar.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The Economy pillar of the party doctrine implies a directing role for the state, inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Personalists reject Marxist utopian abolition of capitalist categories and keep work and labour central.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred from the state-guided economy; not discussed.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Comparisons to Salazar and Franco and the co-management program suggest sympathy, but no explicit corporatist text was found.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Cần Lao doctrine justified vanguard-style party control of the state and army.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: It was a republican regime, though it used Confucian ideas of rule; monarchy is not endorsed.

democracy-best.rationale: Mounier opposed individualistic parliamentary democracy and the regime favoured 'centralized democracy'.

direct-votes.rationale: A party-managed 'centralized democracy' leaves little room for direct lawmaking.

workers-councils.rationale: Personalists reject Marxist class politics, and the party ran the state itself.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inferred from the nation-first and anti-communist national-unity stance.

natural-rulers.rationale: The Confucian element and the intellectual-vanguard party imply a natural moral elite.

political-violence-never.rationale: Nhu endorsed revolution and the party used coercion, so an absolute rejection is unlikely.

war-builds-character.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's moderation theme, though heroic witness appears in Mounier.

separate-church-state.rationale: Catholic influence on the party was strong, and the state was meant to embody the spiritual dimension.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The doctrine was spiritual but multi-confessional (Confucian and Catholic), so scripture-based law is not supported.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred from the idea that the state exists for persons.

military-superiority.rationale: The regime built security forces in a frontline anti-communist war.

ethnic-nation.rationale: 'Bloodline consciousness' tied citizen dignity to lineage, implying an ethnically grounded nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Mounier's personalism explicitly rejected the Marxist reduction of history to class and capital.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Inferred: it cares about material conditions but not as equality of outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from its national-unity focus; not discussed.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anti-colonial but no position on reparations is documented.

civilizational-union.rationale: It built transnational 'spiritual fraternities' and a Third Way network across Asia and Latin America.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Personalism holds the person is a being for others and treats individualism as a defect.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The doctrine rejects both isolated individualism and absorption by the collective, so it holds rights and duties in balance.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The Three Humanities include the individual's relation to nature as part of community.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred from Catholic and family values.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: It criticises materialism but did not reject modern industry, so inferred disagreement.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on moderation in material life.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from the idea of a fixed person with a spiritual dimension.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from the person-centred refusal to treat people as mechanisms.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from the secret-police and surveillance outlook of the regime.

restore-past-order.rationale: It called itself revolutionary and forward-looking, though with traditional elements.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The doctrine was the official ideology organising four pillars of state and party.

direct-action.rationale: Inferred: it sought power through party and state machinery.

means-match-ends.rationale: Mounier's personalism holds that the person cannot be a means to collective ends.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of Marxist utopianism.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Personalists care about need but not as a Marxist distribution principle.

production-for-use.rationale: It criticised profit-driven liberalism and communism alike without adopting a production-for-use model.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Nhu blamed liberal conditions for domination by the rich, but the movement rejected Marxist class analysis.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The doctrine was built to immunise citizens against Marxism-Leninism.

collective-farming.rationale: Nhu condemned communism as repressing everyone under a collective economy.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Inferred: the critique was moral and not a theory of imperialism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Inferred from its collective-responsibility critique of liberal individualism.

harm-principle.rationale: A moral-order doctrine would allow limits beyond harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Personalism sees the person as relational and rejects the isolated individual as bearer of rights alone.

conscription.rationale: The wartime state with a strong army makes conscription consistent.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred from its stress on national belonging.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred; persons are not customers but members of communities.

positive-liberty.rationale: Nhu said liberal freedom leaves workers free in politics but isolated and defenceless in economics.

media-academia-power.rationale: Inferred; the party sought to use the press and education itself.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Bloodline was framed as spiritual and historical lineage, not genetic ability.

organic-representation.rationale: Communitarian personalism favours representation through communities, though the regime used a party.

total-state.rationale: Personalists hold that the state serves the person, though the regime claimed pillars over Spirit and Society.

national-rebirth.rationale: The revolution aimed to rebuild a decolonised nation.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The party worked through secret loyalties and Confucian ties, but this is not stated as a political principle.

bound-labor.rationale: Inferred from its criticism of domination.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The doctrine pursues Truth, Goodness and Beauty as real values.

universal-morality.rationale: The supernatural dimension pursues universal truth, goodness and beauty, with Neo-Thomist roots.

single-common-good.rationale: Personalism posits a communal good for persons, though it is not framed in these terms.

revive-national-language.rationale: Vietnamization of personalism fits cultural revival but the specific policy is inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Co-management of industry by capital and labour representatives is documented as the program.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred from Catholic educational interests; not discussed.

economic-freedom.rationale: Nhu said liberalism's economic freedom enslaves the weak; the link between economic and political freedom is therefore resisted.

rule-by-example.rationale: Its Confucian element stresses moral rulers, though the regime also relied on law and coercion.

national-self-determination.rationale: Personalism was adopted as the ideological basis of an independent, non-communist Vietnamese nationalism.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The doctrine insists on a spiritual and supernatural dimension, with Catholic and spiritualist roots.

class-collaboration.rationale: The party's program favoured co-management by capital and labour, and Catholic unions aimed to harmonise capital and labour.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: It stressed ancestral veneration and national spirit.

dominated-front.rationale: Its Third Way network opposed both blocs yet the regime was allied with the United States.

workers-nation.rationale: Workers were organised within a national Cần Lao party rather than internationally.

ban-interest.rationale: Not an Islamic or scholastic-usury program in the sources.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Inferred from the dignity of every person.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Rejected as part of Marxist materialism.

elite-replacement.rationale: Inferred; conspiratorial claims are not part of the doctrine.

proportional-representation.rationale: Party dominated the assembly; no documented stance.

national-mission.rationale: It sought transnational networks promoting the doctrine against communism.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The party was itself the governing elite and defended it.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred from the inviolable dignity of every person.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The regime's security apparatus was closed to accountability.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Its program included cooperatives, unions and a state Economy pillar.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Personalism treats dignity as intrinsic to every person; equal legal rights are inferred.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not a socialist doctrine in the Marxist sense; no documented view.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Its nationalist doctrine of 1949 spoke of respecting freedom of belief and religion.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Catholic involvement suggests it would accept religious instruction.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The regime held plebiscites and elections, though under a dominant party.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Inferred; it used coercion in service of its goals and does not hold libertarian principle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Personalism stresses communion rather than struggle.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The regime banned communist activity and ran a dominant party.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Nhu criticised workers' domination by the rich under liberalism.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Cần Lao acted as a vanguard-style party in the state, though not a proletarian one.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Nhu stressed protection of workers from domination by the rich.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Class collaboration and party-linked unions suggest limits on adversarial strikes.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The Cần Lao declaration blamed persistent poverty on social conditions despite progress.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Inferred from national spirit and lineage emphasis.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The regime used emergency measures against internal communist enemies.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: State-guided economy makes it plausible; not documented.

party-controls-media.rationale: The party aimed to penetrate the media and used its journal Society.

party-commands-army.rationale: The party placed its members in key army posts.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The party operated through secret cells and strict discipline.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The president was the central power in the regime.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Bishop Ngô Đình Thục led its training centre and it grew from Catholic organisations.

clerical-rule.rationale: Clergy trained cadres but did not rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Inferred from its nationalism and anti-Leninism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred from moral-order emphasis and state spirit pillar.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from dominant presidency and party.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The regime depended on a US alliance.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: No source suggests the doctrine sought to ban renting; inferred disagreement as it is a radical program outside its mixed-economy path.

people-in-arms.rationale: Inferred from the reliance on a regular army.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The doctrine was a counter to the northern regime in a contested divided nation, so reunification aims are inferred.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The party was an intellectual cadre.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: It blended Asian and Western values; no explicit stand.

death-penalty.rationale: The regime applied it; no doctrinal statement.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from Catholic and Confucian ethics.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The Catholic and spiritualist outlook might favour it, but nothing documented says so, so I record no stance.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Bloodline consciousness tied dignity to lineage.

minority-language-support.rationale: Nothing documented; it stressed a national Vietnamese spirit, but no policy on minority languages is recorded.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Nothing documented; freedom of belief was affirmed but exemptions from general law were not discussed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Personalism favours communion and moral order over eccentric individualism.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Nothing documented on international debt; the regime depended on foreign aid but no doctrine addresses repayment.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The republic endorsed personalism in a constitution after a 1955 referendum.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from solidarity themes; the regime relied on US aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The doctrine predates this debate and the regime relied on an ally; no principled stance is documented.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The president of the republic was elected by popular vote and plebiscite under Diệm, an arrangement the doctrine's regime used.

central-bank-independence.rationale: No documented position and the principles point neither way.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Nhu's critique that unlimited economic freedom lets the rich dominate workers implies property is answerable to wider human needs.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Nothing documented; it opposed the Soviet model as materialist, not as capitalist.

collective-defense.rationale: It was part of an anti-communist alliance order in the Cold War.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Catholic clergy and bishops were close to the party, making curbs on religious bodies unlikely.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The president led the party-backed regime and was not a neutral symbol.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred from centralised nation-building; it fought the North's separate system.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Confucian Mandate of Heaven ideas were used but a sacred or divine-descent ruler is not claimed.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from concern about domination by the wealthy.

character-from-environment.rationale: Personalism stresses both nature and conditions without choosing.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine that persons have inviolable dignity before the state.

leader-cult.rationale: Diệm's regime promoted the leader's image; the doctrine's Confucian ethos supports it.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis it rejected wholesale.

land-redistribution.rationale: The sources do not address land reform.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred; no irredentist program is documented.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Its 1949 doctrine of nationalism included respect for freedom of belief.

women-must-cover.rationale: No basis in Confucian-Catholic Vietnamese tradition.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Mounier rejected Marxist materialism for reducing societies and history to capital production and class, and the Vietnamese doctrine kept that stance.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred from opposition to domination by concentrated wealth.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Personalism protects persons against collectives but the regime's courts were not independent.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred; it relied on foreign aid.

moral-incentives.rationale: Moderation and spirit over material incentives are core to the doctrine.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: It promoted workers' revolution through a party organisation and not through guerrilla foco.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred from its republican egalitarian ethos.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Vietnamization stressed Vietnamese historical and spiritual foundations.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The doctrine arose as a postcolonial, anti-colonial nationalism.

patriotic-education.rationale: Personalism training reached about 25,000 officials and doctrine was spread through education.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: It viewed capitalism as flawed but did not predict collapse.

delink-world-market.rationale: The regime relied on integration with the US-led camp.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis foreign to the doctrine.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Contrary to its concern that workers and the weak not be dominated.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The republic's constitution endorsed the Person but no stance on entrenchment is documented.

elective-rulers.rationale: The republic's head of state was elected, as the doctrine's regime practiced.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Confucian mandate ideas support it but regime claims suppress it.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's nature dimension.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from its Catholic social ethos about protecting workers from the rich.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Personalism calls for committed engagement of persons.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Mounier criticised mass culture before the war but the sources give no answer on its class function.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Its authors were compared to Salazar, Franco and Peron and drew on Pétain-era legacies, so it hardly treats antifascism as founding.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: It opposed communism and collectivism; fascism is not addressed directly by its sources.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American historical question outside the doctrine, with no basis for an answer.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Outside the doctrine's concerns; its reverence for ancestors cuts one way, its anti-colonial stance the other.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Outside the doctrine's concerns; no basis in its sources for a stance.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Outside the doctrine's concerns; no basis in its sources for a stance.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Vietnamization aimed to give the doctrine an Asian foundation distinct from Western forms.

military-guardian-role.rationale: It put party members in army posts and relied on the army.

paid-care-work.rationale: Family as a community is valued, but nothing documented addresses paying domestic labour.

filial-duty.rationale: Ancestral veneration was combined with personalism in the doctrine.

office-by-exam.rationale: The Confucian element suggests merit-based mandarin selection, though this is inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: It did not favour collective or communal land ownership as such.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The republic had a national assembly, though the party dominated it.

single-official-language.rationale: Nothing documented; Vietnamization favoured Vietnamese culture but no language law is recorded.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: A modern legal-policy question the doctrine never addressed.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The doctrine said capitalism treats people mainly as consumers, in contrast to the person with spiritual dimensions.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: It built transnational anti-communist networks but arming insurgents is not documented.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Nothing documented; it opposed Soviet influence but this concerns a great power's own bloc.

corporate-influence.rationale: Nhu said the wealthy dominate isolated workers under liberalism.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from nationalism and security concerns.

residents-only-property.rationale: A local housing-policy question with no documented doctrinal stance.

job-guarantee.rationale: Concern for workers is documented but no employment guarantee program is.

democratic-peace.rationale: An international-relations thesis the sources do not discuss.

non-intervention.rationale: No stance documented; it supported anti-communist international networks, which cuts against strict non-intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: It endorsed unionization but not a form.

local-production.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses localism in production.

informal-organisation.rationale: The party was hierarchical and cell-based.

religious-nation.rationale: It was officially multi-confessional with freedom of belief in its nationalist statements.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: A fiscal-federalism question not addressed by the doctrine.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: It would back private belongings but rejected common ownership of production in the collectivist sense.

defeat-communism.rationale: The doctrine was designed to immunise citizens against Marxism-Leninism and mobilise anti-communist networks.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred from a mixed-economy middle path.

religion-illusion.rationale: Personalists contrast Marxist hopes for an earthly paradise with transcendence, and the doctrine had a supernatural dimension.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: It criticised liberalism but did not deny that it had achievements.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The Vietnamization theme favoured national forms, but no language purism is documented.

treaties-binding.rationale: A question about indigenous peoples and states, not addressed by the doctrine.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Cooperatives were endorsed but not as property-holding self-governing communities replacing the state.

majority-settlement.rationale: Nothing documented on internal settlement policy.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Positioned explicitly as a middle ideology between capitalism and communism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Nothing documented on competing claims to territory.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The party aimed at dominant, centralised control and clandestine rule.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic-law question outside the doctrine's Vietnamese, Catholic and Confucian setting.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Co-management gestures at participation but the party controlled the state.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred disagreement from the doctrine's rejection of class-based analysis and its focus on the person and community; not discussed.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic personalist view of inviolable dignity.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The doctrine presented itself as a middle ideology combining elements of both sides.

alienated-labor.rationale: Personalists criticise treating the person as a production tool, though not in Marxist theory.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The doctrine blended Catholic and Confucian ideas of heavenly mandate.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's support for a role for religion in public life; not directly discussed.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A modern employment-law question the doctrine never addressed.

social-market-economy.rationale: The program's cooperatives and co-management with a market base fit this.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The regime was a wartime state.

rich-first.rationale: The doctrine criticised domination by the rich but also backed development; no stance on sequencing is documented.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The regime was aligned with the US bloc.

dynastic-succession.rationale: It was a republic, though the Ngô family monopolised posts.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Cooperatives were endorsed but credit mutualism is not discussed.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The regime relied on foreign aid; no doctrine on lenders' conditions is documented.

property-franchise.rationale: Nhu criticised domination by the rich.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred disagreement: the doctrine values nature and women's family role but does not frame them as shared domination.

reification.rationale: Mounier's critique of having over being is close but the term is Marxist.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Nhu said workers lacked the means to protect themselves from domination by the rich.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Not documented; the regime used both laws and decrees.

online-participation.rationale: The doctrine predates the internet and says nothing on online deliberation.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: No documented stance; it was officially multi-confessional but family-oriented.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Catholic and Confucian adherents divided on this and the sources give no unified answer.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Nhu said liberal freedom left workers dominated by the rich.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The doctrine was built to counter materialism and strengthen belief.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The regime built a security state.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: A consociational-politics question the doctrine never addressed.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: It endorsed cooperatives and unions as well as moral duty, but no preference between charity and state aid is documented.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: A modern concern the doctrine never addressed.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Its church ties were with episcopal Catholic structure.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Not addressed beyond family as community.

rent-control.rationale: No documented housing policy; inferred neither way.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred disagreement from its mixed-economy stance; intellectual property is not discussed.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine and no principle points either way.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: It relied on US support but this is not a doctrinal stance.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the dignity premise would support recognising mass killing but the political question is separate.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Labour was central to the party's identity, and it criticised rule by owners.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from realism of a wartime state.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Bloodline consciousness tied dignity to historical lineage.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from the natural-order, family-centred anthropology of the doctrine; not discussed.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's traditional family and gender norms; not discussed.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Mounier stressed heroic witness; the nation-survival theme supports honouring those who die.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Nhu likened liberalism and communism to Satan's temptation, framing politics as spiritual.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine had no program on diasporas.

culture-before-state.rationale: Spirit was the first of its four pillars and Vietnamization aimed at cultural renewal.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic and Confucian traditions behind it; the sources do not discuss feminist reading of texts.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Nothing documented on redrawing administrative regions.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Inferred from Nhu's wish that workers not be dependent on the rich and from cooperative ownership; the sources document no property distribution program.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from Nhu's view that formal freedom without economic protection is hollow; the sources do not apply this to national independence directly.

person-over-state.rationale: Nhu called the person the supreme value of all societies, and personalism rejects both individualism and collectivism on this ground.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The doctrine's central charge against capitalism and communism is that each reduces people to a material role, and it aims at material and spiritual moderation.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from the Cần Lao Party's practice of organising labour under party-led unions and co-management; the doctrine's own texts do not state it.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred: Nhu rejected Marxist materialism and offered a personalist middle path, but wrote nothing on what counts as socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine stresses cooperatives and a mixed economy but the sources say nothing on local services.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from the centralised, dominant-party design and the unicameral National Assembly of the Republic of Vietnam; the sources do not discuss chambers.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: the party favoured cooperatives, co-management and state direction, not ownership by local communities.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The party practised centralised democracy and a vanguard-style dominant-party state, the opposite of leaving decisions to local assemblies.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from Catholic labour thought and Confucian family ethics that shaped the doctrine; no source states a wage position.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Inferred: nothing in the sources bears on medical regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred: nothing in the sources bears on anti-ageing research.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the regime's secret-cell, surveillance-minded and state-directed economy, which would not accept payments beyond state control.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the regime's security-minded dominant-party practice; the doctrine predates the internet.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from the centralised democracy of the Cần Lao Party and the Diệm government, which left no entrenched regional power.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine predates genetic engineering and its principles give no direction.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine says nothing on settlement patterns or the environment.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred: its nationalism rests on Vietnamese national and bloodline consciousness, not on organising by race within politics.

racial-pride.rationale: The doctrine's nationalism includes a bloodline consciousness of Vietnamese ancestry, so pride in ancestry fits, though racial pride is not stated as such.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from its anti-communist posture of defending South Vietnam; the sources do not state a rule on use of force.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred from Nhu's nationalism and the Vietnamese-personalist emphasis on the national community; the sources do not discuss language as the definition of a nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine envisages one unified national community under a dominant party state, with no place for separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred from the regime's anti-communist nationalism and its framing of the division of Vietnam as imposed from outside; the sources do not state a partition plot.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred: the personalist stress on education of the person suggests support, but the sources do not discuss tuition.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not discussed in the sources, and the doctrine's middle path between capitalism and communism gives no stated position on pollution taxes.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the personalist and Catholic-Confucian emphasis on the continuity of the community across generations; the sources do not state it directly.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; Mounier's personalism does not claim distinct values for women, and the regime's Women's Solidarity Movement was nationalist in practice.

arms-reduction.rationale: Not discussed in the sources, and the regime was committed to a large anti-communist army, so there is no stated position.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the regime's closed, authoritarian one-party practice, which did not favour open government, but the doctrine itself does not address diplomacy.

capital-controls.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; the regime relied on American aid, and the doctrine's middle path gives no stated view on capital flows.

missingStatements.text: The state exists to serve the person, and no person may be treated merely as a means to the ends of the community or the state.
missingStatements.rationale: Nhu called the person the supreme value of all societies, and personalism rejects both individualism and collectivism on this ground.

missingStatements.text: Human beings have a spiritual as well as a material nature, and politics should serve both.
missingStatements.rationale: The doctrine's central charge against capitalism and communism is that each reduces people to a material role, and it aims at material and spiritual moderation.

notes: Documentary base is thin and partly regime-written. Answers on the regime's practice (security, one-party control, media) may be more authoritarian than the doctrine's text; Western personalists such as Mounier later accepted liberal democracy. Catholic and Confucian emphases varied among its cadres.
